title: Groupe de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux (jusqu’en été 1969) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continued from p.12): K is a complete discretely valued field of characteristic 0 with perfect residue field k of characteristic p, and I is the inertia group. For an abelian variety A_K, φ_A(σ) = Tr(σ | T_ℓ A) for σ in I. This trace is independent of ℓ (SGA 7 IX), so it may be computed with any ℓ ≠ p. On p.12 Grothendieck tested whether the 'character' of a Barsotti–Tate group on prime-to-p inertia elements is determined by its p-torsion M(0) = pM. Brauer lifting together with M = Z_p(1) shows this fails when μ_p ⊄ K. He then asks whether it can hold when μ_p ⊂ K.

This page states the test question. Suppose μ_p ⊂ K and A_K[p] is a constant group (inertia acts trivially on A[p]). Is φ_A(σ) = 2·dim A, i.e. the trivial value, for all σ in I of order prime to p?

By Grothendieck's monodromy theorem, φ_A on prime-to-p elements detects the finite quotient Φ = I/I_{K'} through which I acts on the 'abelian part' of T_ℓ. Over the minimal extension K' giving semi-stable reduction, the toric and abelian parts are acted on by Φ. So the question is the p-adic analogue of Raynaud's criterion (SGA 7 IX 4.7): if A[n] is rational over K for some n ≥ 3 with p ∤ n, then A has semi-stable reduction. Grothendieck asks whether this survives for n = p when μ_p ⊂ K, and notes that only non-semi-stable reduction is at issue.

Elliptic-curve case, p ≥ 5:
- Take K' minimal with semi-stable reduction.
- Then G = Gal(K'/K) restricted to inertia embeds in Aut(E_{s'}), which is μ_2, μ_4 or μ_6. This group is cyclic of order prime to p, so K'/K is tame.
- The question becomes whether φ_E ≡ 2 on prime-to-p inertia (equivalently G = 1) whenever E[p] is constant and μ_p ⊂ K.
- Multiplicative or ordinary reduction is harmless: the étale quotient of T_p carries a tame character ψ^{-1} of order m prime to p, and ψ ≡ 1 mod p forces ψ = 1. Hence only the case where the reduced curve over K' is supersingular (Hasse invariant 0) remains.

The margin marks this as a question for Tate.
errors: The typed text says the trace should equal n = dim A_K. On T_ℓ (rank 2·dim A) the trivial value is 2·dim A. The elliptic-curve paragraph itself uses 2, so this is a slip.
The claim that only the supersingular reduced curve needs checking is correct for semi-stable/ordinary reasons, but it is asserted without argument (easy argument given in the reconstruction).

The question is left open. A plausible negative answer for highly ramified K: take E with good supersingular reduction whose p-torsion has inertia acting by a ramified quadratic character χ, and form the twist E^χ. Since μ_p ⊂ K gives e ≥ p-1, Raynaud's bound e < p-1 no longer constrains finite flat models, so such E may well exist. This is not verified here.

ideas.what: Trace of prime-to-p inertia on T_ℓ is independent of ℓ and computable via any ℓ; it detects the semi-stability defect group
ideas.modern_name: ℓ-independence of inertia traces / Serre–Tate, Grothendieck monodromy

ideas.what: Question whether Raynaud's semi-stable reduction criterion (A[n] rational, n ≥ 3, p ∤ n) extends to n = p when μ_p ⊂ K
ideas.modern_name: p-adic analogue of Raynaud's criterion for semistable reduction
ideas.usually_credited_to: Raynaud criterion: SGA 7 IX 4.7; later variants by Silverberg–Zarhin (1990s)
ideas.where_published: Unsure whether this exact question appears in print

ideas.what: For elliptic curves with p ≥ 5, the defect group is cyclic of order 2, 4 or 6, and only potentially supersingular reduction is problematic
ideas.modern_name: Semistability defect (Kraus), tame potentially good reduction

missed.claim: Grothendieck poses a concrete test question: does full constant p-torsion (with μ_p ⊂ K) force semi-stable reduction? He reduces it, for elliptic curves with p ≥ 5, to curves with potentially supersingular reduction and flags it for Tate. This is the case e ≥ p-1, outside Raynaud's finite flat uniqueness range.
missed.quote: il faudrait ici trouver un exemple où le critère de réduction semi-stable de Raynaud est en défaut pour ℓ = p !
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The p-torsion version of the semi-stability criterion in the large-ramification regime ties to modern potentially crystalline mod p theory (Breuil–Kisin modules, inertial types). An explicit answer or counterexample is not standard textbook knowledge, though it is probably known to experts.

deep.surprise_reason: A natural, explicitly posed question (p-adic Raynaud criterion) with a correct reduction to the supersingular case. It is interesting historically but routine for specialists and likely settled implicitly by later p-adic Hodge theory.
